projects.title: What Mile?
projects.description: Interactive geospatial guessing game for the Appalachian Trail. Players identify locations on a map with scoring based on trail-mile accuracy.
projects.learned: Geospatial UX is tricky — making a map game feel intuitive on mobile required rethinking every interaction.

projects.title: Tiny Doodle
projects.description: A delightfully simple drawing app designed for children, featuring daily creative prompts. Built with React and designed for COPPA compliance. Minimal interface, maximum creativity.
projects.learned: Designing for children requires ruthless simplicity. Every feature must pass the 'can a 5-year-old figure this out?' test.

projects.title: Carbon Tracker
projects.description: Browser widget helping users understand their web browsing carbon footprint through data visualization and behavioral insights.
projects.learned: Carbon data is messy and inconsistent. Building trust in the numbers is as important as the numbers themselves.

projects.title: Wild Blue Travel
projects.description: SEO and growth consulting for an adventure travel company. Performed technical audit, restructured content strategy, and implemented schema markup to improve search visibility.
projects.learned: Results: 3x organic traffic growth in 6 months. 45% increase in qualified lead submissions.

projects.title: jamesburney.com
projects.description: This site — vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, no frameworks. Dark mode, service worker, low-power mode detection, accessibility-first design.
projects.learned: Constraints breed creativity. Building without frameworks forces deeper understanding of web fundamentals.
